title: One-Stop Ops Ecosystem Guide: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates company-wide operational policies and end-to-end processes that touch access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and reusable internal templates. The goal is to reduce cross-team ambiguity, shorten approval cycles, and enforce minimum compliance & security standards while preserving developer velocity.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor representatives who interact with production or sensitive systems.
- Covers cloud & on-prem resources, vendor-supplied services, and any expense or procurement action initiated on behalf of Redwood.

Primary service references (examples)

- Identity & Access: Okta (SSO), AWS IAM, GCP IAM, internal RBAC service (redwood-auth).
- Secrets & Keys: HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS (customer keys where required), HSM-backed key stores for Restricted data.
- Procurement & Expenses: ProcureFlow (internal procurement portal), Concur (travel & expense), Stripe/Adyen for payments.
- Change & Ticketing: Jira (change requests), PagerDuty (oncall routing), Confluence (document storage).

Roles & Responsibilities

- Requester: Initiates requests (access, change, purchase, travel). Responsible for accurate justification and cost coding.
- Approver: Assigned manager or budget owner; must validate business need and security posture.
- Security Reviewer: Reviews high-risk access, vendor security questionnaires, and data handling clauses.
- Procurements Team (Finance): Runs vendor onboarding, issues POs, validates contracts.
- Platform/Infra Owner: Executes changes or grants system-level access; responsible for operational testing and rollback procedures.

Access & Permissions

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; grant only the permissions necessary for the task.
- Time-bound access for most high-privilege grants; default max of 72 hours unless business case provided.
- Separation of duties: staff who approve changes should not be the only ones making them in production for critical systems.

Request process (standard flow):
1) Requester fills the Access Request template in ProcureFlow/Confluence (use the template at end of this doc).
2) Request is routed to Requester’s Manager for approval (SLA: 48 business hours).
3) If resource is flagged "Sensitive" or "Restricted" (see Data Classification) Security Reviewer is cc'd and must approve (SLA: 24 business hours).
4) Platform Owner implements the grant and records evidence (timestamp, approver id, change id).

Expedited/Emergency access:
- For urgent incidents, request via PagerDuty incident channel with an Emergency Access ticket in Jira. Emergency grants are logged and must be reviewed in the next 72-hour post-incident review.

RBAC matrix (simplified)

| Role | Typical permissions | Access duration | Approval path |
|------|---------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Viewer | Read-only dashboards, logs | 6 months | Manager auto-approve |
| Developer | Deploy to non-prod, read prod metrics | 90 days | Manager approval |
| Oncall Engineer | Escalation, runbooks, limited prod run commands | 30 days (auto-rotate) | SRE lead approve |
| Admin / SRE | Create/destroy infra, token minting | 72 hours default, require MFA & hardware key | Manager + Security |

Helpful CLI example (internal):

redwood-ops-cli request-access --resource arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/prod-readonly --reason "Investigate latency spike" --duration 4h

(Outputs a Jira change request link and creates an audit entry in Vault audit log.)

Change Management

Classification:
- Minor: Non-user-facing, low-risk config changes (no approval required beyond owner).
- Standard: User-facing or infra changes that require manager approval and a scheduled window.
- Major: Releases, database schema changes, or anything touching PII or Restricted data. Requires change advisory board (CAB) review.
- Emergency: Incident-driven, followed by postmortem and retroactive CAB notification.

Change windows and SLOs:
- Standard change review SLA: 3 business days for routine approvals.
- Deployment rollback detection: monitor for 5-minute error spike > 3x baseline; automatic rollback policy triggers if threshold persists for 15 minutes.

Rollout patterns and minimum telemetry:
- Canary: 5–10% traffic for minimum 10 minutes, monitor latency (p95), error rate, and key business metrics.
- Gradual ramp: 25% → 50% → 100% with 15–30 minute guardrails at each step.
- Feature flags should be used for user-facing changes; use LaunchDarkly or internal flag service.

Emergency change workflow (short):
1) Create Emergency Change ticket in Jira with "EMERG" tag.
2) Notify oncall via PagerDuty.
3) Apply minimal change and validate.
4) Open post-incident review within 72 hours; CAB to record decision and any permanent changes.

Data Management

Classification tiers (company-wide):
- Public: Information intended for external publication.
- Internal: Company operational data; default for most internal documents.
- Sensitive: Customer-identifiable data, analytics derived from identifiable users. Requires encryption at rest & transit, access audits.
- Restricted: PII, PHI, regulated data. Requires HSM-backed keys, monthly access review, and two-person access approvals for exports.

Data retention & backup policy:
- Critical logs: 365 days online, 5 years in cold storage (S3 Glacier).
- Production DB snapshots: Daily snapshots retained for 30 days, weekly snapshots retained for 6 months, monthly for 3 years (if required by contract).
- Backups verification: Restore test quarterly for each critical service; Platform team owns verification and records it in the quarterly Ops report.

Encryption & key management:
- All Sensitive/Restricted data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256. Keys for Restricted must be KMS-backed and rotate at least every 365 days.
- Secrets stored only in HashiCorp Vault; secrets rotation policy: database credentials rotate every 30 days by default.

Data sharing & exports:
- Exports of Sensitive/Restricted data require documented business justification, Security sign-off, and a temporary export token with a max TTL of 2 hours.

Procurement & Expenses

Principles:
- Centralized vendor onboarding for any vendor with access to company systems or any expected spend > $5k.
- Purchase Order (PO) required for capitalized hardware or any contract > $10k annually.
- Card-level expenses for travel and small purchases follow Concur workflows with receipts.

Approval matrix (examples):
- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000–$10,000: Department manager approval and budget code.
- >$10,000: Finance (Procurements Team) + Legal review for contract terms.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum):
1) Completed vendor security questionnaire (VSA).
2) Contract template signed (SLA, liability, data handling, termination).
3) PO issued (if applicable).
4) Technical contact listed and access provisioning plan documented.
5) Insurance & compliance evidence collected.

Common procurement steps (short form):
1) Create procurement request in ProcureFlow with justification and budget code.
2) Manager approves per matrix.
3) Finance verifies vendor standing and issues PO.
4) Legal signs contract if required.
5) Platform configures vendor access per onboarding plan.

Expense & travel specific rules:
- Nightly hotel rate cap (domestic): $300/night unless pre-approved.
- Meal per diem: $60/day domestic; actuals reimbursed with receipts up to policy limits for international travel.
- Mileage reimbursed at IRS / local statutory rate; file through Concur within 30 days.

Vendor Management

Ongoing oversight:
- Quarterly vendor risk reviews for vendors with production access or > $25k annual spend.
- Security posture checks: penetration test evidence, SOC2 report, ISO27001 where relevant.
- SLAs & remediation: Vendors must commit to incident notification within 4 hours for security incidents affecting Redwood.

Offboarding:
- Access revocation must be coordinated between Platform Owner and Vendor Management team.
- Verify data return/destruction clauses executed.
- Perform asset inventory reconciliation: credentials, SSH keys, API keys revoked, and confirmed in Vault audit logs.

Travel Policy (high level)

Booking & approvals:
- All travel must be booked via ProcureFlow/Concur with pre-approval for international travel.
- Managers approve travel based on business justification and budget.

Health, safety & security:
- For travel to high-risk regions, additional Security clearance and travel advisory review are required. Reach out to security@redwood.ai for approvals.

Templates & Attachments

This section contains short, copy-and-paste templates for common requests. Insert into ProcureFlow or Confluence forms as required.

1) Access Request (short form)

- Title: Access Request — [resource] — [team]
- Requester: [name] / [email]
- Resource: [ARN / service name / URL]
- Justification: [business reason]
- Duration requested: [hours / days]
- Approver: [manager name]
- Security impact: [None / Sensitive / Restricted]

2) Change Request (Jira summary)

- Summary: [Service] — [Change type] — [Planned UTC window]
- Description: Technical plan, rollout steps, monitoring queries, rollback steps, stakeholder list, impacted customers.
- Verification criteria: exact metrics (p95 latency < X ms, error rate < Y%) and smoke-test checklist.

3) Vendor Onboarding Checklist (to attach)

- Company legal name:
- Contract owner (Finance):
- Security questionnaire link:
- PO number:
- Prod access plan (yes/no): details

Example: Access Request CLI payload (JSON)

{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/prod-readonly",
  "reason": "Investigate perf regression",
  "duration_hours": "4"
}

Audit & Reporting

- Monthly access review: managers receive an automated summary of active grants and must certify or revoke.
- Quarterly compliance report: Finance+Security produce a report summarizing vendor posture, high-risk access, and unresolved findings.
